speaker: fitz
text: Woodpeckers bang their heads into trees thousands of times a day.

speaker: fitz
text:
Easy. Its skull is a built-in shock absorber.
But scientists filmed woodpeckers in slow motion. The beak and head stopped together. No cushion.

speaker: fitz
text:
Padding would soften every hit. You don't pad a hammer.
So the trick is size. Their brains are hundreds of times smaller than ours. And smaller brains handle bigger jolts.

speaker: gauge
text: So being small is the helmet!
